content: Patients who receive vaccinations within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated approximately three months after discontinuing therapy, provided their immune competence has been restored. Chloroquine can increase the levels or effects of haloperidol by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism and may also increase haloperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Similarly, histrelin can increase chloroquine toxicity via QTc interval prolongation, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine can elevate hydrocodone levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to its analgesic effects. Chloroquine also increases hydromorphone levels or effects through CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary in both cases. Chloroquine increases iloperidone levels or effects by altering CYP2D6 metabolism, while iloperidone can elevate chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may increase plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases imipramine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. It also reduces the efficacy of the trivalent recombinant influenza virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially decreasing immune response in immunocompromised individuals. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of inotuzumab, isradipine, and lenvatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Close ECG monitoring is advised when lenvatinib is co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. Caution and monitoring are necessary in all cases. Chloroquine levels are increased by istradefylline, which affects CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect is not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Lanthanum carbonate reduces chloroquine levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Chloroquine should be administered at least two hours before or after lanthanum. Similarly, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and sodium bicarbonate decrease chloroquine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Doses should be separated by at least four hours. Lenacapavir increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions to CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of leuprolide, levofloxacin, lofexidine, and lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary in all cases. Lorcaserin increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Lorlatinib decreases chloroquine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of morphine, metoprolol, mexiletine, and methamphetamine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Mifepristone increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Mirabegron increases chloroquine levels by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Mitotane decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer, and dosage adjustments may be required for co-administered CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin, nilotinib, and nortriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. It also increases nortriptyline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine and ofatumumab SC may increase each other's immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. The additive effects on the immune system should be considered when co-administering immunosuppressive therapies. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of olanzapine and olaparib by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents may potentiate and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Close monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is essential, and subsequent doses should be titrated accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, oliceridine dosage may need to be increased until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ondansetron, osilodrostat, and osimertinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Oxaliplatin increases chloroquine levels through an unspecified mechanism. ECG changes should be monitored if therapy is initiated with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of oxycodone and oxymorphone by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of paliperidone, posaconazole, and ribociclib by prolonging the QTc interval. Ribociclib also increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of risperidone, romidepsin, and vemurafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rolapitant increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Rolapitant may elevate plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates for at least 28 days following administration. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine decreases the effects of sipuleucel-T and zoster vaccine recombinant due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce vaccine effectiveness. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of tacrolimus and thioridazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine decreases the effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, reducing the conversion to its active metabolite, endoxifen. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the levels of tamsulosin by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness if co-administered. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Terbinafine increases chloroquine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of torsades de pointes-inducing drugs such as triptorelin, valbenazine, and vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine decreases the effects of vaccines such as influenza virus vaccine trivalent, meningococcal group B vaccine, and rabies vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may interfere with the development of active immunity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine, ibutilide, and iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6, such as paroxetine, perphenazine, and promethazine, by decreasing their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine decreases the effects of pneumococcal vaccines and hepatitis vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of QTc-prolonging drugs such as pasireotide, pentamidine, and posaconazole. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine decreases the effects of praziquantel through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6, such as duloxetine, encainide, and fluoxetine, by decreasing their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of QTc-prolonging drugs such as eribulin, ezogabine, and formoterol. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine decreases the effects of live vaccines such as measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce vaccine effectiveness. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of QTc-prolonging drugs such as mefloquine, mifepristone, and octreotide. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of drugs metabolized by CYP2D6, such as loratadine, maprotiline, and paroxetine, by decreasing their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of QTc-prolonging drugs such as rilpivirine, sotalol, and tacrolimus. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
